title: The Pros and Cons of Organic Farming | Ecology and Environment | Biology | FuseSchool
summary: School science video on the downsides of organic farming: lower yields and more land, higher dairy methane, mixed environmental footprint, and organic farms still using natural and some synthetic pesticides.

assertions.quote: the yields are lower because More Produce is damaged by pests
a liter of organic milk requires 80% more land than conventional milk to produce
organic is not necessarily better for the environment either
organic dairy farms do actually produce more methane per cow than conventional Farms because of the diet of the cattle

verdicts.note: Forage-heavy diets raise methane per unit of milk in many studies, but per-cow and per-farm comparisons are mixed.

assertions.quote: It is actually a big misconception that Organic Farms cannot use any pesticides
organic farmers can use both synthetic and natural kinds of pesticides
as fewer chemicals are used there is less risk of chemicals remaining in the food
organic in one country could allow more chemicals than are allowed even in conventional farming in other countries
